summary: A capstone is judged on the quality of the decision and on how honestly it is measured, not only on whether the code runs.
Write a four-part problem statement and measurable objectives that name the metric.
A data project is a pipeline of six stages; each arrow can fail, so name the failure of each.
Accuracy can lie. With 23 percent failures, doing nothing is 77 percent accurate and useless.
Try the cheapest method first and screen the idea for consent, bias and human review before coding.
Keep a data sheet for every dataset and say clearly when the data is simulated.

summary: Document every column in a data sheet: meaning, unit, range, source and whether it is known at prediction time.
Five faults appear in nearly all data: missing, impossible, duplicate, inconsistent and outlier values; clean them in code and print counts.
Scale features with z-scores and check correlations; a weak feature is a finding, not a failure.
Split into train, validation and test with stratification; use the test set once.
A suspiciously good feature signals leakage: information that is not available when the prediction is made.
Protect people: anonymise, limit access and say when data is simulated.

summary: Logistic regression turns a weighted score into a probability with the sigmoid; gradient descent learns the weights by reducing log loss.
Read the loss curve and both training and validation scores; a large gap signals over-fitting.
Weights of correlated features are associations, not causes.
Tune the threshold on validation, then report the test set once with the confusion matrix, precision, recall, F1, AUC and precision at the top, next to the baselines.
Use cross-validation for a steadier estimate and a bootstrap interval to judge group gaps.
A fairness paragraph states the groups checked, the numbers and, just as important, what was not checked.

summary: Save the model as a small versioned file and wrap it in a function that validates input and returns the model version.
Eight fast tests, including behaviour tests and a save-load round trip, make the service trustworthy.
Drift has two forms: inputs change (covariate) or the relationship changes (concept). PSI watches inputs; only outcomes reveal concept drift.
An alarm means investigate; retrain by a rule written in advance.
A system about students needs consent, minimisation, access control, retention limits and human review.
Describe deployment honestly: laptop demo, college server, cloud tier, and a manual fallback.

summary: Follow your college's report format first; use the 70-page map as a budget check that favours data, evaluation and ethics.
Posters and slides use claims as titles, big numbers, baselines beside results, and a limit.
Plan an 8-minute talk with a protected question slot and a controlled demo with a backup.
A similarity checker cannot prove originality; understand and cite everything, and be open about AI assistance.
Prepare twelve viva answers, including honest ones about limits, leakage, fairness and privacy.
Score yourself against a rubric before the defence and write a one-page reflection afterwards.
